title: Student Protests Disrupt Hundreds of Schools in France
summary:
Thousands of students in France have been protesting about education standards. The protests began last week in the capital, Paris, and have spread across the country. Cities including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille have been affected.

Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said 735 of France's 3,700 schools were affected "one way or another." He said the situation had "gone from high-school student demonstrations to a public order disturbance." That means some protests have turned into disorder, and police have been called in.

Education Minister Édouard Geffray said the movement had been taken over by people who were not students. He told a French broadcaster that teachers had said, "the people in front of me were not my students." The education ministry said "significant damage" had been done to school facilities, such as gates, entrances and fences. It also said at least 65 staff members were hurt.

A 16-year-old protester named Lola told the AFP news agency that her school was closed that morning. She said police actions had made students angrier.

The protests come six months before France's next presidential election, a crucial time for President Emmanuel Macron.
why_it_matters: Schools are an important public service, so large protests that close or disrupt many of them show how strongly people can disagree about education.
